Label: Video — What is a database in under 4 minutes (Linux Academy, 3 min 47 s)
What it is: The shortest sound introduction to the subject of the course: what a database is, why a spreadsheet stops being enough, and the main kinds of database. A good first video before any detail.

Label: Video — SQL Explained in 100 Seconds (Fireship, about 2 min 30 s)
What it is: A fast preview of the language that learning outcomes 3 and 4 are about: tables, keys, and the shape of a query. Watch it once now and again after Class 2.

Label: Video — Introduction to Database Management Systems (Neso Academy, 11 min 3 s)
What it is: Defines data, information, database and DBMS one after the other, in the same order as this lesson, on a whiteboard and at a beginner's pace.

Label: Video — Database Tutorial for Beginners (Lucid Software, 5 min 32 s)
What it is: Starts from a spreadsheet that has outgrown itself and shows, with drawings, why the same data are safer in tables managed by a DBMS. It prepares the vocabulary of Classes 3 and 4.

Label: Video — 7 Database Paradigms (Fireship, 9 min 53 s)
What it is: The closest single video to this lesson: key-value, wide-column, document, relational and graph databases, each with its data model, its typical use and a product name, in under ten minutes.

Label: Video — Big Data In 5 Minutes | What Is Big Data? (Simplilearn, about 5 min)
What it is: Explains what makes data 'big' and why one machine stops being enough, with one worked example of splitting the work among several machines. It prepares Class 12.

Label: Video — How does a blockchain work - Simply Explained (Simply Explained, 5 min 59 s)
What it is: Blocks, hashes and the chain between them, and why the alteration of one block is detected, in six minutes and without any talk of prices.
